objectives.title: Development standards
objectives.statement: Build agents to consistent standards, with a written statement of the job, tests written from that statement, and then the code.
objectives.risk: Inconsistent quality that is costly to maintain
objectives.metric: Share of builds that meet the development standards
tiers: The experiment follows the team's own practice.
The build has a written statement of the job and tests before it is released.
The tests are written from the statement before the code, by someone other than the code's author.
Each stage of the build is held by a named person or agent and leaves a signed record.
objectives.evidence: The statement, the tests and the record of who held each stage.

objectives.title: Quality gates
objectives.statement: Require every agent to pass set quality gates before it can be deployed.
objectives.metric: Share of releases that passed every gate
tiers: No gate applies inside the sandbox.
Automated tests and checks must pass before release.
A reviewer who is not the author approves the release after the automated gates pass.
Gate results are signed into the release record, and a failed gate can only be overridden by the executive sponsor.
objectives.evidence: The gate results attached to the release record.

objectives.title: Security review of the code
objectives.statement: Scan and review every agent's code for security weaknesses before it is deployed.
objectives.metric: Share of releases with a completed security scan and review
tiers: The experiment is scanned with the standard tools.
Static scanning runs on every build, and serious findings block the release.
A security reviewer who is not the author reviews the code, and dynamic testing runs before release.
Findings and their resolution are signed into the release record and reviewed by an outside party each year.
objectives.evidence: Scan results and the security review for the version that is running.

objectives.title: Test coverage
objectives.statement: Test agents enough to find defects early, with unit, integration and behavior tests that include what the agent must refuse.
objectives.metric: Share of declared offerings and refusals covered by tests
tiers: The experiment has the tests its builder judges useful.
Each declared offering has at least one test.
Each offering and each refusal is tested, including tests that try to make the agent act outside its scope.
Tests include adversarial cases, and the suite is reviewed by someone outside the building team.
objectives.evidence: The test suite, its coverage of the declaration, and its results for the current version.

objectives.title: Approved release pipelines
objectives.statement: Deploy only through approved pipelines, so that what runs is exactly what was approved, with no edits by hand.
objectives.metric: Share of deployments made through an approved pipeline
tiers: The experiment may be deployed by hand inside the sandbox.
Every production deployment goes through an approved pipeline.
The running agent's fingerprint is checked against the approved release, and a mismatch stops it.
No person can change a running Tier 4 agent outside the pipeline, and attempts are recorded.
objectives.evidence: Pipeline logs, and the comparison of the running fingerprint with the approved release.

objectives.title: Documentation
objectives.statement: Document every agent, including its design decisions, its interfaces and how to operate it, and keep the documents in step with the version that runs.
objectives.risk: Agents nobody else can run or fix
objectives.metric: Share of agents that meet the documentation standard
tiers: The experiment has a short description of what it does.
The agent has interface documentation and an operating guide.
The documentation is gathered from the agent's own declarations, so it cannot say more than they do.
The documentation is reviewed at each release by the people who operate the agent.
objectives.evidence: The documentation for the current version, and the date it was last generated or reviewed.

objectives.title: Dependency security
objectives.statement: Take each dependency from a known source, pin it to a version, and check it for known vulnerabilities, again whenever new ones are published.
objectives.metric: Known vulnerabilities in dependencies, by age
tiers: Dependencies come from the organization's approved sources.
Every dependency is pinned, and known vulnerabilities are checked at each build.
Dependencies are verified by checksum or signature, and new vulnerabilities trigger a review within a set time.
Serious vulnerabilities must be fixed or accepted by the executive sponsor within a set time, and the record is audited.
objectives.evidence: The pinned dependency list, the verification results and the vulnerability scan history.

objectives.title: Signed build record and bill of materials
objectives.statement: Give each package a signed record of what went into it and who held each stage, including every library, model and outside tool it uses at an exact version.
objectives.risk: Nobody can say what is inside a running agent
objectives.metric: Share of releases with a signed build record and bill of materials
tiers: The experiment lists its main components.
Each release has a bill of materials.
Each release has a signed build record, and building the same source again gives the same package.
The build record is published to the parties who rely on the agent, and an outside auditor can verify it.
objectives.evidence: The signed build record and bill of materials for the version that is running.

objectives.title: Models and prompts pinned
objectives.statement: Record the model and the prompts each agent runs on, so that a model update or a prompt edit is a change like any other and goes through the same gates.
objectives.risk: Behavior that changes without a release
objectives.metric: Share of agents with their model and prompts pinned in the release
tiers: The experiment notes which model it uses.
The model version and the prompts are part of the release.
A new model version or prompt is released only after the evaluation suite passes against it.
Model and prompt changes are reviewed by the value owner as well as the builders.
objectives.evidence: The model version and prompt fingerprints in the release record, and the evaluation run for each change.
